findings.title: The optional pidfd launch can follow an expired deadline
findings.expected: Each process-creation attempt is preceded by an absolute deadline check after potentially blocking preparation.
findings.observed: Before trying the optional pidfd launcher the code first resolves it with dlsym. glibc serializes lookup with concurrent library changes. The deadline check before the helper precedes that lock. The ordinary posix_spawn fallback has its own check.
findings.impact: If lookup takes the remaining budget, the first launch attempt can start after the deadline. Later disposal and collection still apply.
findings.recommendedFix: Recheck the existing deadline after symbol resolution and immediately before using the optional launcher.
findings.requiredVerification: Exercise deadline exhaustion between an independently controlled symbol-resolution result and the attempted launch.

findings.title: The target matrix still describes Linux-only stack test machinery
findings.expected: The matrix names each stack probe and its actual release-profile job.
findings.observed: The general description says the tests read /proc/self/mem. The macOS and Windows probes read with their native APIs. Their rows also omit the current optimized stack tests.
findings.impact: The table gives incorrect per-target evidence and can hide real optimized runs when reconciling CI.
findings.recommendedFix: Name each backend probe and include the optimized stack step on Apple and Windows rows.
findings.requiredVerification: Check both Apple and both Windows logs and the Linux branch against the revised table.

findings.title: The API guide overstates the Android io_uring read-back
findings.expected: Distinguish installed restrictions from platform-specific runtime probes.
findings.observed: The API guide groups Linux and Android together for new socket and io_uring checks. The filter denies the relevant calls on Android, while the explicit io_uring probe is Linux-only to avoid the device policy terminating a test call.
findings.impact: Readers can overestimate what runtime verification establishes on Android.
findings.recommendedFix: Identify the Android filter rule and Linux-only runtime read-back separately.
findings.requiredVerification: Check the API wording against the filter and target cfg of the probe.

findings.title: The macOS terminal threat documentation uses an absolute claim
findings.expected: Describe what the profile relies on and the limits of the terminal evidence.
findings.observed: The security policy says the sandbox cannot refuse TIOCSTI on its own. The implementation deliberately relies on controlling-terminal separation and the technical guide records a refusal in the checked scenario.
findings.impact: The absolute claim obscures the conditions that the separate worker boundary actually establishes.
findings.recommendedFix: State that the protection relies on avoiding a controlling terminal, and qualify the observed refusal by its test conditions.
findings.requiredVerification: Read the security and technical descriptions together with the Unix terminal branch and native test setup.

remediation.evidence: Before trying the optional pidfd launcher the code first resolves it with dlsym. glibc serializes lookup with concurrent library changes. The deadline check before the helper precedes that lock. The ordinary posix_spawn fallback has its own check.
The general description says the tests read /proc/self/mem. The macOS and Windows probes read with their native APIs. Their rows also omit the current optimized stack tests.

The API guide groups Linux and Android together for new socket and io_uring checks. The filter denies the relevant calls on Android, while the explicit io_uring probe is Linux-only to avoid the device policy terminating a test call.

The security policy says the sandbox cannot refuse TIOCSTI on its own. The implementation deliberately relies on controlling-terminal separation and the technical guide records a refusal in the checked scenario.

limitations: The six short release campaign results for this candidate are missing. The long GitHub campaign is a later tag stage. Local campaigns were left stopped. Tagged provenance and attestation are evaluated during the tagged phase.
Android, iOS, iOS Simulator and ARMv5 are compile-only in this evidence and have no app/device run. Native host Linux tests cannot supply those platform guarantees.

On the hosted Linux runners the nested PID namespace subcase is partial. Two i686 secretmem cases are ignored. Real Windows console and the named macOS access-list, mount and special folder probes remain unverified.
Native optimized stack tests use the Rust test harness. The test report covers the measured wipe paths and does not establish linked panic-abort, hardware erasure or general side-channel resistance.

Miri was limited to portable operations without native OS interaction. ASan excludes the four native lock assertions that its own lock interceptor changes, and leak checking is disabled. See individual runtime logs.
Cargo-deny bans and sources and RustSec cached advisories were checked separately. The offline cargo-deny advisory database checkout is missing.
Cargo careful, Kani and loom are not installed in the workspace toolchain. Native OS authority was checked by source and applicable platform tests.

Approval review blocked executing the external cargo-semver-checks binary again, despite its registry install record and the offline baseline. AUD-024 retains the earlier default verification; this audit does not claim a fresh exact-candidate run.
The source was audited with lexical site inventories. The per-site semantic/runtime evidence ledger and re-execution of every earlier conditional case remain incomplete.

The initial TSan protected-stack test fails its OS lock read-back under a runtime that explicitly ignores mlock. The separate synthetic concurrent probe covers four public stack and buffer allocations with the supported assertions.
